title: M-C Clockwork Balance
lede: Register six → read their six → bring the three that attack their structure while preserving your Mega for the matchup that needs it.
philosophy: This six wins through positioning, controlled switching, and one protected win condition rather than bringing the same three every game. Salamence is the Mega resource, while Primarina and Aegislash stabilize matchups and Garchomp, Meowscarada, and Hippowdon flex into the opponent's structure. Preview their strongest pressure first, then choose the three that make their preferred attacks awkward.
meta: Regulation M-C Singles rewards flexible cores around high-usage threats such as Salamence, Garchomp, Primarina, Aegislash, Meowscarada, and Hippowdon. This six uses those roles as a preview toolbox instead of forcing one fixed trio.
setsNote: Use 66 SP on every Pokémon with no stat above 32. Mega Salamence is the primary Mega, but do not Mega it automatically; preview decides whether its speed, power, or defensive profile is the resource you need.

packs.label: Switch Punisher
packs.when: Their six is passive, slow, or dependent on one defensive core.
packs.identity: Meowscarada removes items while Garchomp and Salamence punish the switches that follow.

strategy.opponentPattern: Their six relies on defensive switching and a small number of answers to physical pressure.
strategy.purpose: Meowscarada strips items and creates U-turn momentum, Garchomp punishes Steel and Electric answers, and Salamence threatens a setup finish.
targets: teams with limited Ice or Fairy coverage
strategy.winCondition: Remove or weaken the defensive items and Salamence checks, then use Dragon Dance to finish.

pilot.thesis: Make every defensive switch cost either an item, health, or positioning.
pilot.rule: Use Meowscarada to reveal the answer, then send the correct breaker.
pilot.fail: Do not lock the team into attacking the same wall when U-turn gives a better route.

packs.meta: This is the dedicated bullying package for previews where the opponent has a slow defensive shell.
packs.philosophy: The goal is not to brute-force the wall immediately. Remove its item, force it to switch, and punish the structure around it.

switches.send: Meowscarada — Flower Trick threatens immediate damage.
Meowscarada — Knock Off creates immediate pressure.
Garchomp — Earthquake punishes Steel answers.
Garchomp — Ground immunity blocks the attack.
Salamence — Intimidate and Flying typing can create the switch.
Salamence — Flying typing avoids Ground attacks.

plan.title: Clock
plan.goal: Remove the item that makes their wall difficult to break.
plan.play: Lead or pivot Meowscarada into the passive target and use Knock Off.
plan.next: Bring the breaker that attacks the exposed response.

plan.title: Shield
plan.goal: Preserve Salamence until its checks are identified.
plan.play: Use Garchomp to pressure Steel and Electric answers.
plan.next: Stop attacking the wall when the opponent is forced into their Salamence answer.

plan.title: Clean
plan.goal: Use Mega Salamence to punish the final defensive sequence.
plan.play: Dragon Dance after the opponent's main answer is weakened.

loops.title: Item-to-breaker loop
loops.body: Meowscarada removes an item. The opponent switches to the expected answer. Garchomp punishes that answer. Salamence enters once the defensive chain is weakened.

victims.name: Passive balance
victims.why: Knock Off, U-turn, and Stealth Rock turn their repeated switches into permanent losses.

victims.name: Slow defensive cores
victims.why: Meowscarada acts before most walls and prevents them from controlling the pace.

counters.name: Fast offense
counters.why: Use Tempo because this package can be overwhelmed before its setup plan begins.

counters.name: Ice-heavy structures
counters.why: Use Core because Salamence and Garchomp become liabilities when Ice pressure is abundant.

advantages.title: Item removal
advantages.body: Removing one key item can change whether Salamence needs one Dragon Dance or two.
advantages.watch: Identify Leftovers, Heavy-Duty Boots, Focus Sash, and Choice items.
advantages.play: Use Knock Off early when the target depends on its item.
advantages.rule: Never waste Knock Off on a disposable item when the true defensive item is still hidden.

hazards.title: Ice coverage
hazards.body: Both Garchomp and Salamence can be punished by Ice attacks.
hazards.watch: Count every Ice move and Ice-type attacker before choosing Bully.
hazards.play: Keep Meowscarada and a healthy defensive alternative available.
hazards.rule: Never bring Bully when their six has multiple reliable Ice users unless the payoff is clear.

pilot.thesis: Use preview to choose the three that make the opponent's preferred structure uncomfortable, then win through controlled switches and one protected closer.
pilot.rule: Core is the default; Tempo answers speed, Anchor answers physical and Electric pressure, and Bully attacks passive structures.
pilot.fail: Never bring the same three automatically. If their six changes the threat pattern, change your three.

plan.title: Clock

plan.play: Lead the anchor that makes their first attack least rewarding.
plan.next: Use the revealed information to choose your first switch.

plan.title: Shield
plan.goal: Preserve the two Pokémon that answer their strongest threats.
plan.play: Cycle the anchors and punish predictable switches instead of trading blindly.

plan.play: Mega Evolve Salamence only when Dragon Dance creates a decisive position.

advantages.title: Preview toolbox
advantages.body: The six contains three different ways to attack the opponent's structure rather than one fixed team.
advantages.watch: Count their Ice, Fairy, Electric, Fighting, and priority answers before selecting three.
advantages.play: Choose Core for balanced threats, Tempo for speed, Anchor for physical or Electric pressure, and Bully for passive structures.
advantages.rule: Never select three based only on your favorite Pokémon.

advantages.title: Mega resource
advantages.body: Mega Salamence is strongest when the opponent has already revealed its checks.
advantages.watch: Identify their fastest revenge killer and strongest Fairy or Ice answer.
advantages.play: Delay Mega Evolution until it changes a matchup or enables a clean.
advantages.rule: Never treat Mega Evolution as an automatic first-turn action.

loops.title: Balance triangle
loops.body: Identify the attack. Send the anchor that absorbs it. Observe the response. Switch to the Pokémon that attacks that response. Repeat until Salamence has a clean setup turn.

hazards.title: Ice into the Dragons
hazards.body: Garchomp and Salamence share a dangerous Ice weakness.
hazards.watch: Count every Ice attacker and every Pokémon carrying Ice coverage during preview.
hazards.play: Prefer Primarina and Aegislash as the first answers and avoid exposing both Dragons.
hazards.rule: Never send Garchomp or Salamence into a known Ice attack.

hazards.title: Hazard overload
hazards.body: Repeated switching can turn balance into a losing race if hazards stay on the field.
hazards.watch: Notice whether their six can stack or maintain hazards.
hazards.play: Favor Tempo when immediate pressure prevents repeated switching and avoid unnecessary pivots.
hazards.rule: Never make three defensive switches in a row when hazards are accumulating.
